newsitem.title: UK: Phillips Intl 1996 auction sales up 16 percent.
newsitem.headline: Phillips Intl 1996 auction sales up 16 percent.

text.p: Britain's Philips International Auctioneers & Valuers said on Thursday that its turnover for 1996 rose 16 percent to 113.51 million stg from 97.59 million in the previous year.
Phillips' chairman Christopher Weston said its expansion in Europe played a crucial role in its growth with its turnover in Geneva rising 49 percent.
It had acquired a permanent saleroom in Geneva during the year, with a staff of specialists managing the centre.
Phillips, a leader in philatelic auctions, completed sale of the "Alphonse collection' for four million stg.

Among some of the rare items sold by Phillips in 1996 were a sea hunter's hat from the Aleutian Islands which fetched 78,500 stg, a cricket bat used by Australia's Sir Don Bradman which sold for 23,000 stg and a lost leaf from George Washington's undelievered inaugural address which went for 199,500 stg.
